scientific.integrity: The primary full text was inspected at the model assumptions, multinomial contagion derivation, hypergeometric contact-count statement, reproduction-number approximation, and simulation setup. The predecessor SIR paper was inspected at its contact assumptions and explicit binomial-approximation qualifier. The earlier SEIHR extension was inspected through its contact definition, approximation step, and transition law. The bundled checker evaluates the exact finite-population formula independently. Independent audit has not been performed.
scientific.limitations: The finding corrects the exact finite-population contact law. It does not claim a material change to the source's reported large-population simulation tables, and the large-population reproduction-number approximation remains correct to first order. If repeated contacts are intended, the multinomial contagion formula can be retained but the hypergeometric contact-count assertion must be replaced by a binomial law.

title: The finite-population contact law in a stochastic COVID model is internally inconsistent
